summary: Apply automatic Core IOThreads and bounded VirtIO network multiqueue without frontend settings

guide.reason: Document automatic defaults and how existing VMs receive them during stopped saves, including guest queue activation limits.

api.reason: Existing authenticated vm-create/vm-update commands and result/inventory contracts carry unchanged VM specifications; Core generates and verifies native device defaults. No endpoint or wire field added.

roadmap.reason: A bounded Core default improvement does not close any platform phase or performance acceptance gate.

state.reason: Automatic defaults persist only with the existing Core-managed VM configuration.
state.record: The pool master retains the VM specification and ownership in pool-vms. The assigned Core retains exact applied XML in managed journal Domain and libvirt persistent configuration. A fresh Controller adopts the VM through managed inventory without regenerating devices or re-entering tuning.

verification.method: Full Go race suite, final vmhost race suite, API reference/contracts, privacy and syntax checks passed. Native nested KVM creation, hotplug, Controller replacement, stopped save and last-SCSI removal passed. A retained four-arm workload capture shows higher throughput with material receive retransmissions; the separate channel-limit diagnostic produced no samples, and production performance qualification remains open. Independent review verified code, documentation and all retained numeric evidence. Two unrelated pre-existing CI-string assertions fail in the broad Python suite. See scoped QA for exact evidence and limits.
